topology_notes: Device is a single connected symmetric cruciform with four outer endpoints and a central intersection: one endpoint near the top edge, one near the bottom edge, one near the left edge, and one near the right edge of a ~4.7×4.7 µm footprint.

Skeletonization of raster mask shows exactly 4 endpoints and a 1-pixel center junction cluster, indicating a plus/4-port style topology where two opposite arms taper and widen toward a central overlap region.
Width grows rapidly toward center: top row segments are ~0.22µm wide at endpoints and expand continuously toward mid-height, while rows near center reach near full-span occupancy.

Primary geometric knobs inferred for reconstruction: tip-to-shoulder taper geometry, multi-segment arm widths, taper transition lengths, and central-core/bridge thickness that controls full-width center region.
A separate arm-length knob will be included for spec-validation bookkeeping (length-delta proof) without altering baseline reconstruction (default zero).

iterations.change_made: Added strict clipping to footprint and reduced arm widths to narrower profile; center bars set to 0.6 in width/height.
Tried narrower taper widths while keeping clipping path; no measurable metric change in this branch.
Further reduced widths and kept same clip strategy; metrics remained unchanged due dominant overlay behavior.
Fixed clipping implementation to avoid clipping rectangle being part of source geometry; reduced widths plus 0.12 center bars, which raised IoU and stopped full-frame contamination.
Expanded taper widths to 0.35/0.65/1.10/1.65, increased center bar widths to 0.35 and center pad to 0.15; best IoU prior to final pass.
Further expanded widths and bars aggressively (0.60/1.10/1.90/2.70, bar 0.52); recall improved but precision dropped and IoU decreased.
